bullets: Game 6 of 6 in a single-deck session (video 1305.3-1593.9s): Mighty Miner, Cannon, Skeletons, Evo Baby Dragon, Lightning, Electro Spirit, Evo Royal Hogs, The Log (3.25 average elixir) against a log-bait variant with Firecracker, Golden Knight, Inferno Tower, Tornado, Evo Skeleton Army, Skeleton Barrel, Royal Delivery and The Log. He sight-reads the list before it appears: "I know this guy plays like a weird log bait variation... I think he has like golden knight and inferno tower, too" (1310-1320s).

The deck wins on spell chip, not on a push. Four Lightnings each take exactly 423 HP off the enemy right tower (4858 -> 4435 at 1332s, 3727 -> 3304 at 1504s, 3304 -> 2881 at 1560s, 2881 -> 2458 at 1572s), about 1700 of the 2400 total damage; Royal Hogs nibbles supply the rest (4435 -> 4199 at 1436s, 4450 -> 3727 at 1466-1468s). Stated plan: "I can just continue lightning his inferno towers over and over again. Sometimes even like lightning his firecrackers and stuff cuz there's no reason not to" (1421-1427s).

Royal Hogs are used three ways in one game: back-placed at [2, 2] when the opponent cannot punish (1320.3s), pushed at the bridge purely to drag out the Skeleton Army or Inferno Tower ("We have to force it out anyways", 1458-1460s; "evo piggies here forces out the inferno tower. Just get elixir out of him", 1563-1566s), and once as a defensive blocker ("Piggies here to block the firecracker", 1542-1544s).

Defence is a cheap rotation - Cannon at [10, 8] / [10, 12] / [11, 11] / [10, 11] / [8, 10] roughly every 30s, plus Skeletons, Electro Spirit, The Log and the Evo Baby Dragon - and Mighty Miner is used as a bridge threat rather than a defender (labels at [15, 15] at t=1398.4, 1474.5, 1551.5). He keeps The Log unspent against a barrel deck: "I don't want to log. I need to save the log here" (1469-1471s).

Cycle advantage is stated twice and never contested: "We did outcycle him" (1431s) and "Let's log here. We don't get out cycled by him either" (1502-1505s). No crown falls on either side in the readable window (final towers own 4468 / 4024, enemy 4740 / 2458); he calls it at 1583s ("Okay, yep. It's just over") and closes the video at 1586s: "Very nice win. Thank you all for watching." Win.

new_deck.rationale: A 3.25-elixir list built on a fast win condition (Evo Royal Hogs) plus one-elixir cycle cards (Skeletons, Electro Spirit) and The Log, but it wins by defending with Cannon, Mighty Miner and Evo Baby Dragon and chipping with repeated Lightning rather than by out-pushing.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every card in the list answers something in a bait or small-troop deck for less elixir than it costs the opponent: Cannon and Skeletons hold ground win conditions, Electro Spirit and Evo Baby Dragon clear swarms and Firecrackers, and Mighty Miner is a bridge threat that also deletes tanks. That leaves Lightning free to be used as a chip spell on whatever defensive building or ranged troop the opponent commits - four casts in this game each took 423 HP off the same tower. Royal Hogs are rarely a kill attempt; they are an elixir pump that forces the Skeleton Army or Inferno Tower out and takes a nibble or two while doing it, which is exactly how Ryley states the plan: "the more elixir I force out of him, he's just completely unable to go in or just able to build up any type of pressure" (1566-1572s). The weakness the game never tests is a heavy beatdown push: the deck has no big ground answer other than Mighty Miner plus Cannon.
